At BOOTING the game re-checks only six rules: `PLACEMENT_DEF_UNKNOWN`, `SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT` (EM:665: the authoring lint and boot refuse any other self-powered fixture; the dock status glows of DA-46 are counted by `DOCK_GLOW_COUNT` instead, recognised by their `node_ref` list until the Emitter's amendment names their class, so BOOT never refuses them, OQ-DA-46, user ruling X2 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `BEACON_COUNT`, `STORY_SLOT_LIST` (Layout's), `RESIDUAL_LIGHT_COUNT` and `DEAD_FAULT_NOT_DRIED`. The structural lint is Layout's BOOTING pass and is cited, never re-listed. A failed CI content lint never bricks a release boot beyond that subset. The lint is a **pure function of the files plus one named config**: every threshold it reads lives in `content_lint_config`, rows `{name, value, owner, status in {LOCKED, PLACEHOLDER}}`; `TUNING_SOURCE_DRIFT` compares each LOCKED row with the registry and each PLACEHOLDER row with the owner GDD's current text, so a placeholder cannot silently become a fact. The PLACEHOLDER rows this GDD reads from other owners (each a `content_lint_config` row with status PLACEHOLDER, never LOCKED) include `MAX_EMITTERS` (Emitter), `BEACON_SWEEP_TICKS` (Emitter), `LANTERN_LIGHTS_MAX`, `NONSHADOW_LIGHTS_MAX`, `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` and `OCCLUDER_POLYS_VIEW_MAX` (Lighting) and `GLOWSTICK_STACK_MAX` (Item DB), beside the rows already so marked in the text. Output is ordered by `(template_id, lint_id, record_key)` ascending and two runs over the same bytes produce identical bytes; waivers are rows `{lint_id, record_key, reason, owner}` in the same file, a waiver without a reason is an ERROR, and `frame_exception` and the PD-1 exceptions are waivers of this form (no waiver may name `STORY_SLOT_FILLED_IN_MVP`). -> ADR candidate: the lint runner's shape, language and location.
638	
639	**Lint tranches (design review 2026-10-27).** The 90-row table *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up; Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: was 88, plus `DECISION_REACH_MISSING` and `DWELL_BUDGET_LOW`)* is delivered in tranches so CI can be turned on early: **T0** the six BOOT rules; **T1, the minimum CI set**, the ERROR rows that guard the shipped data (`AUTHORED_NON_INTEGER`, `SPAWN_BLOCKED`, `SELF_POWERED_LAMP_COUNT`, `BEACON_COUNT`, `RESIDUAL_LEDGER_CLOSED`, `FAULT_COUNT_EIGHT`, `ORPHAN_LOW_HP`, `POWER_TREE_MISSING`, `OVERLOAD_WINDOW`, `EMPTY_WINDOW`, `FROZEN_ROOM_UNFORCED`, `COLD_ROOM_UNDECLARED`, `COLD_WORK_BUDGET`, `RETURN_PATH_TRAVERSE`, `ESCAPE_ROUTE_OVER_BUDGET`, `FIXTURE_COUNT_ROOM`, `FIXTURE_COUNT_WORLD`, `TRAVERSE_TOO_LONG`, `TUNING_SOURCE_DRIFT`, `STORY_SLOT_FILLED_IN_MVP`); **T2** the remaining ERROR rows (`DWELL_BUDGET_LOW` is T2 and runs red on the current content plan until the plan adds dwell sources, D.23, OQ-DA-56; `DECISION_REACH_MISSING` joins T2 as an ERROR once the spike fixes the geometry); **T3** the WARN rows and the ASSET rows. A tranche is complete when its rows run clean on the three shipped templates, and a later tranche never blocks an earlier one *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*.
640	
641	**DA-42 Content acceptance runs as headless tests, not lint.** Rules that need the Graph to run are integration tests in `tests/integration/derelict_authoring/` using the kernel's headless path (H10): `G0_ZERO_PART_SURVIVABLE` (IDB AC-42: a patch-only run of all eight faults ends none FAILED or DESTROYED, including the case "`v_o2_cryo` never opened", which passes because the isolated duct holds its `hp` (gated, DA-16), and the case "seam breaker closed onto a dead B" with its re-open recovery, `G0_SEAM_CLOSED_ON_DEAD_B`, DA-20) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, `G0_SCRUBBER_INSTALL` (a scrubber installed in a home slot with `j_cryo` closed, recovered by opening `j_cryo` and a zero-part PATCH, DA-47) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `FAULT_D15_DRIFT` (each live fault within +-15 % of the Graph's D.15 at its trigger), `DEAD_FAULT_STILL_REPAIRABLE` (every dry dead fault is still repairable, at its authored `hp`, after `T_SORTIE_LOADED_MAX` minutes of loaded idle, because gated wear holds it; and the flowing-time ledger itself is asserted: `pb_leak` repairable at 15.0 min and DESTROYED at 15.3 min of flowing time counted from V12, with the reservoir topped up past step 2,112, where B's own 16,000 mL runs out, D.21) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, `WELD_WITHOUT_PLATE_SURVIVABLE` (welding B with no plate and patching only keeps `seg_b_pump_n` from staying below `BREACH_HP` for more than 60 s at a 3.5-minute patch cadence) and `SCRAM_RESTART_STEADY` (patch `pb_leak`, then V12: `r_b` reaches RUNNING and does not re-SCRAM in 10 minutes; skip the patch and the stock crosses the floor at step 1,238 after V12 and `r_b` SCRAMs again after it and by step 1,826, about 1,588 expected, D.21 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*). The harness shape is an ADR candidate; they are tagged (auto) in Acceptance Criteria.
642	
643	**DA-43 The authoring workflow (data first; editor tooling deferred).** (1) The floor plan is drawn as an ASCII grid in `tools/asset-pipeline/plans/<template_id>.txt` (one character per 48 px tile, half-tile walls on the 24 px lattice per LY-3). (2) A converter turns the grid into `tile_runs`, wall runs and the rect table. (3) Placements, nodes, fixtures, faults and ledgers are hand-written records. (4) The offline lint runs Layout's structural rules, then this GDD's CONTENT rules. (5) The template is written to `assets/data/sections/`. **Plan grammar (minimum, normative until the converter ADR lands) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*:** one character per 48 px tile; a letter per `room_key`, as in the C.1 to C.3 drawings; `+` a door position on the wall run it sits in; `-` a corridor tile; `H` a socket hatch; a space is exterior; `x:` and `y` header rows carry tile indices; the 24 px wall strips and the hull runs are derived by the converter and never drawn. Jogs, hull-segment and plate-position marks and loose-slot marks belong to the converter ADR, and **that ADR is a prerequisite of the first template story**, because without it TEMPLATE_DRAFT to TEMPLATE_CONVERTED is unspecified. **Positions live in the template files:** every anchor, fixture, hardpoint, plate position, loose slot and route length is a record there, the figures in this GDD are design values, and acceptance criteria check "within +-48 px of the template value". **Proposed story split** (for `/create-stories`; the effort is XL): S1 plan grammar ADR and converter; S2 lint runner, tranches T0 and T1 (DA-41); S3 headless harness and the G-0 family; S4 `home_ship`; S5 `derelict_a`; S6 `derelict_b` and the weld; S7 kit manifest and the `_worn` atlas; S8 lint tranches T2 and T3; S9 playtest rounds X-DA-1 to X-DA-10. A Godot editor exporter (an `@tool` or EditorPlugin route) is deferred to an ADR and a spike. **Engine feasibility:** the pinned reference has no scripting, core, editor or tools module (`docs/engine-reference/godot/modules/` covers animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui only), so every claim about JSON loading, editor tooling, TileMapLayer authoring and export filters is `[UNV]`: `JSON.parse_string` returning floats (cast and bound-check every authored integer), the export include filter for `assets/data/**/*.json` (a 30-minute spike against the 4.7.2 export templates, IDB OQ 23) and a 4.7 typed-return override rule for any loader or lint base class are the items to verify. -> ADR candidates: authoring tool pipeline and the offline lint runner; headless content harness; worn-atlas derivation tool; atlas selection by `template_id` in the PROJECTOR. This GDD describes behaviour and data shape, never code.
644	
645	**DA-44 Template edits and registry discipline.** A template edit changes its `template_hash` (LY-26 drift policy); saves before the first external build are disposable (SL-14) and template migration begins only after it. A `room_key` change is committed only with a note in the file header. Registry discipline: owner-named values that are not registry entries (`ESCAPE_ROUTE_BUDGET_PX`, `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE`, `MAX_STORY_SLOTS_PER_SECTION`, `DOOR_CORNER_MARGIN_PX`, `TILES_WORLD_MVP`, `SOCKET_SPACING_MIN_TILES`) are cited by owner GDD and rule and never minted here; `INTERACT_FIXTURE_BUDGET` (Interaction) and `part_cover_pm` (Item DB F-11, with its band as variables) are registry entries and are cited by name and registry value; `FREEZE_ON_MC` -20000 is a registry entry (Graph-owned), as are `LEAK_HP` and `BREACH_HP` 4000. The final stage registers only this GDD's own artefacts, from the final text: the template roster (`template_id` values) (registry: `mvp_template_roster`), the `visible_unknown` record, the MVP fixture-count table (citing LY D.16) (registry: `mvp_fixture_counts`), the fault-allocation table (registry: `mvp_fault_allocation`), the MVP ledger instance (citing IDB F-11) (registry: `mvp_part_ledger`), the legal loaded sets of DA-32 (registry: `legal_loaded_sets`), the content lint id list (registry: `content_lint_ids`), the kit-manifest schema name (registry: `kit_manifest_schema`) and the `_worn` token (registry: `worn_variant_token`); the 36 `pending referenced_by` comments become real `referenced_by` entries. (`RESERVE_S` 90 and `INSUL_MC` 5000 were registered by Suit & Equipment after this list was first drawn; they are cited as registry entries, with Suit's placeholder tags kept at each mention.)
646	
647	**DA-45 The first ten minutes are content-shaped (MVP onboarding).** MVP onboarding is the cryo-bay fixture and a hand-led sequence the layout supports; there is no scripted tutorial and no marker. The player wakes with one guttering EMERGENCY lamp; closes the cryo breaker `j_cryo` (V3); the room warms at about 4 mC per Graph step gross (500 W into C = 42 x `C_TILE` 3000 = 126,000 dJ/°C, LSG D.7), about 3 mC net of hull loss at 13 exposed tiles, so about 6.5 minutes (about 3,900 Graph steps) from -2000 mC to COMFORT at 10000 mC; LSG:839's 2.5 minutes is its 20-tile example (D.18); follows the frost trail from `p_cryo_rad` to the failed fitting; patches it (V1). **V5 is first taught here** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `v_o2_cryo` stands shut on the wall beside `door_cryo_s`, in the same sweep as the door and clear of its approach square and of the coolant floor run, and the bay's own air with the door and the valve both shut reaches THIN at 7.0 minutes (D.19; the Graph's atmosphere descriptor, no new tell), a few minutes after the warm-up and the patch, so a player who lingers meets the thinning air with the valve in view. Opening it (V5) restores the bay's supply, starts the hiss at the bare duct and arms O2-SHIP, so the first valve a player turns is a lever with a price, and the answer to the price is the zero-part patch (D.19); a player who leaves through the door never needs it, which is the point of a lever. The cryo-bay door opens onto a lit corridor with the beacon dark; the engine-room door `door_engine_n` stands open (DA-16) and the ember glow of the Fuel Ember row at the `pf_feed` flange is the next thing in view. Later onboarding (Vertical Slice) replaces the hand lead with the Onboarding system. **The first sortie's dwell is content-shaped too** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, Boarding & Salvage D.1, D73)*: the concept's five-minute W_LOOP leaves about 190 s of discretionary dwell that the content, and nothing else, must produce on the way to `htr_a` and back (witnesses read per room, decision points, door choices, stick or lantern pauses); `DWELL_BUDGET_LOW` (D.23) holds the plan to `A_DWELL_BUDGET_MIN_S` 190 s, and nobody tunes the route length or `V_CARRY` to hit five minutes.

479	**DA-32 Loaded sets and subject budgets.** (registry: `legal_loaded_sets`) World-total lints run per *reachable loaded set*, not over the triple (Layout D.16's wording is "over the loaded set"; the Interaction subject cap and the Emitter caps are per loaded set). The sets follow the weld graph: a set is the home body plus at most one unwelded derelict being visited, where the home body is `{home}` before the weld and `{home, B}` after it. (provisional — Web Map & Transit undesigned; orchestrator ruling: R9's three sets are replaced by the systems-designer's five, because B stays loaded as part of the home body after the weld, so a post-weld sortie to A is reachable.)
480	
481	| Set | Meaning | Tiles (`TILES_WORLD_MVP` 600, WARN at 540) | Fixtures (cap 28) | Lanterns (cap 20) | Interaction subjects `S_int` = F + L_seed + C (cap 120 `[PLACEHOLDER: Interaction]`) | `S_total` = S_int + 30 (cap 192 `[PLACEHOLDER: Emitter]`) |
482	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
483	| S0 `{home}` | the wake | 182 | 8 | 3 | 50 + 2 + 18 = 70 | 100 |
484	| S1 `{home, A}` | sortie to A | 300 | 14 | 5 | 78 + 6 + 18 = 102 | 132 |
485	| S2 `{home, B}` | sortie to B (unwelded) | 331 | 15 | 6 | 90 + 5 + 18 = 113 | 143 |
486	| S3 `{home+B}` | welded, no sortie | 331 | 15 | 6 | 90 + 5 + 18 = 113 | 143 |
487	| **S4 `{home+B, A}`** | post-weld sortie to A | 449 | 21 | 8 | 118 + 9 + 18 = **145** | 175 |

489	`F` is the declared interactables (hardpoints, two face subjects per door, valves, hull segments, sockets): home 50 (48 + the two scrubber slots of DA-47), A 28, B 40; `C` is the cap-stub worst case (at most 6 modules x 3 ports = 18); the constant 30 is `PLAYER_DROP_RESERVE` 24 + actors 4 + horrors 2 (`HORROR_SUBJECTS_MAX` `[PLACEHOLDER: Horror]`; registry `subject_budget`). **Fuel is non-binding in MVP (the one depleting consumable without a clock of its own)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Stocks: `ft_main` 20,000 mL (full), `ft_b` 10,000 mL, none on A. Burn is `FUEL_UML_PER_W` 120 micro-mL per served W per step (LSG): the home reactor at its standing 1880 W burns 0.2256 mL per step, a runway of about 88,650 steps = **about 148 minutes**; `r_b` serving B's 1240 W burns 0.1488 mL per step, about 67,200 steps = **about 112 minutes**; after the weld with both running each reactor delivers 1560 W (DA-20), about 0.187 mL per step, so the pooled runway is longer still. Both runways exceed any MVP session, so fuel never binds by burn; the fuel clock that does bind is the FUEL-DRIP leak (fault #4, 1 mL per step at `hp` 3999 and growing as the flange wears while unpatched, LSG D.15 FUEL-DRIP), which the patch treadmill holds. AC-DA-112 asserts the stocks.

**DA-36 Count tolerance is one-sided.** LS-26's "about" counts (nodes about 40 / 30 / 35; edges about 55 / 45; LOADs about 8) are targets, not bounds. `NODE_COUNT_DRIFT` (WARN) fires only when `authored > target + max(floor(target x NODE_DRIFT_PCT / 100), NODE_DRIFT_ABS_MIN)` with `NODE_DRIFT_PCT` 20 and `NODE_DRIFT_ABS_MIN` 3; a count below target is INFO, because the Graph's cost model (LSG D.16) is monotone in count, so fewer is never a defect (Formula D.2). The hard bounds are the Graph's: total authored nodes at most 120 (LSG:787; 104 here), `MAX_GRAPH_NODES` 4096 / edges 8192 (registry, irrelevant at this scale), and the 800-node content WARN (LSG:915; irrelevant at MVP scale, said so). Also lints from the Graph's content-lint criterion: the D.12 fragility sum per compartment (`FRAGILITY_SUM`, WARN above 500,000 ppm), `delta_T_eq` per heated compartment (`HEATER_DELTA_T`, WARN above 60 C; the home cryo bay's single heater is the case checked), and any liquid pipe authored below `FREEZE_ON_MC` without `forced_mode` FREEZE (`FROZEN_ROOM_UNFORCED`, ERROR, CI: any PIPE, RESERVOIR, RADIATOR or liquid tank in a room whose `T0` is below `FREEZE_ON_MC`, DA-40).

**DA-37 Nothing authored is a marker, a lie or a combat placement.** In MVP, no label, icon, arrow, rating or text on any authored piece (VA-13; VA-13's ban targets UI-like markers, not future diegetic lore fragments, which are the narrative-director's to define and would enter through `story_slots`, never as a marker); no "phantom", "false door", "fake trail" or "decoy" record in any template (the Perception Filter corrupts the module-body channel at runtime, never the data); no entity, weapon or enemy placement (tools repel); no loot roll, rarity or tier; no meter, minimap or HUD icon for the visible unknown; no flesh (hue 5 to 30, S 20 to 60 %, V 45 to 85 %) or violet (hue 270 to 330, S above 25 %) pixel in any kit sheet or item sprite, and the lit sample of Hull Grey under every Tungsten source stays at hue 36 degrees or more (`PALETTE_SANITY_BAND`, asset-level, ERROR). A wreck is monochrome before power returns: the chromatic content of a derelict frame is closed to the player's beam, the residual lamp, thrown Chemlight pools, live fault glows and the dock status glow of DA-46 (a dim point inside a dock room only, at a luminance ceiling below the residual lamp's) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (AC-V2 is the measurable form of "darkness is honest"). The anti-pillar guard rails of Player Fantasy are enforced by these lints and by the review checks in Acceptance Criteria.

#### G. The kit, the lint and the workflow

**DA-38 The kit manifest is data, shaped for procgen.** The manifest (registry: `kit_manifest_schema`) is a table of rows `{piece_id, category, footprint_cell, layer, flags, variant_tokens, layout_record_kind, count_bucket}`; no row names a template, so the Vertical Slice generator (VS-A) assembles from the same rows. Categories: floor, wall, door, pipe mount, fixture housing, machinery node, prop, storytelling (empty at MVP), breached variant, shared. Cells follow art bible 8.2 (floor 48 x 48; wall 48 x 96 = face 72 + cap 24; door frame plus leaf 96 x 96; machinery node 96 x 96 with a moving-medium region of at least 16 x 16; props 48 x 48, 48 x 96, 96 x 48; seam bead 4 px Hull Grey). Layers are floor, wall face, cap and prop; flags are `SOLID`, `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` and pipe-band clearance; variant tokens are `_worn`, `_breached`, `_frosted`, `_open`, `_smashed` and the door states. This GDD does not restate LY-4's field tables: it names the record kind a piece instantiates.

689	### States and Transitions
690	
691	Authoring has **no runtime state** (DA-1): nothing here is a state block and nothing is hashed by Authoring. The states below are (1) the lifecycle of a template as a content artefact and (2) the states of authored subjects whose *initial* value this GDD writes and whose *transitions* belong to the owner named in the last column. The point of listing them is to say who may cause each change and to make every authored initial state one of the values the owner already defines.
692	
693	**Template lifecycle (content states).**
694	
695	| State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Transitions | Who may cause them |
696	|---|---|---|---|---|
697	| `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` | a plan file `tools/asset-pipeline/plans/<template_id>.txt` exists, or any edit to a shipped template | the converter runs without error | to `TEMPLATE_CONVERTED` | the level-designer (author) |
698	| `TEMPLATE_CONVERTED` | `tile_runs`, wall runs and the rect table are produced | Layout's structural lint reports zero ERROR | to `TEMPLATE_LINTED`; back to `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` on any ERROR | the converter; Layout's lint (CI) |
699	| `TEMPLATE_LINTED` | the structural lint passes | the full CONTENT lint (DA-40) reports zero ERROR | to `TEMPLATE_CONTENT_CLEAN`; back to draft on any ERROR | the CONTENT lint (CI) |
700	| `TEMPLATE_CONTENT_CLEAN` | the CONTENT lint passes (WARNs listed, not blocking) | the six-rule BOOT subset (DA-41) passes inside a build | to `TEMPLATE_SHIPPED` | the build / CI |
701	| `TEMPLATE_SHIPPED` | the file is in `assets/data/sections/` and its `template_hash` is recorded | any edit | to `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` (new `template_hash`; saves before the first external build are disposable, SL-14) | the author only; never at runtime (LY-2) |

706	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
707	| Fault (live or dead) | `LATENT` | held by a lever at build: a closed valve (flow only, DA-16), an open breaker, a thin margin, an absent load, or an absent weld | the lever is released | to `ACTIVE` when the player or the weld releases it; PWR-OVL on installing a heater; O2-ROOM on the weld | the player (V3, V5, install, V9); Assembly (the weld) |

### States and Transitions

Authoring has **no runtime state** (DA-1): nothing here is a state block and nothing is hashed by Authoring. The states below are (1) the lifecycle of a template as a content artefact and (2) the states of authored subjects whose *initial* value this GDD writes and whose *transitions* belong to the owner named in the last column. The point of listing them is to say who may cause each change and to make every authored initial state one of the values the owner already defines.

**Template lifecycle (content states).**

| State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Transitions | Who may cause them |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` | a plan file `tools/asset-pipeline/plans/<template_id>.txt` exists, or any edit to a shipped template | the converter runs without error | to `TEMPLATE_CONVERTED` | the level-designer (author) |
| `TEMPLATE_CONVERTED` | `tile_runs`, wall runs and the rect table are produced | Layout's structural lint reports zero ERROR | to `TEMPLATE_LINTED`; back to `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` on any ERROR | the converter; Layout's lint (CI) |
| `TEMPLATE_LINTED` | the structural lint passes | the full CONTENT lint (DA-40) reports zero ERROR | to `TEMPLATE_CONTENT_CLEAN`; back to draft on any ERROR | the CONTENT lint (CI) |
| `TEMPLATE_CONTENT_CLEAN` | the CONTENT lint passes (WARNs listed, not blocking) | the six-rule BOOT subset (DA-41) passes inside a build | to `TEMPLATE_SHIPPED` | the build / CI |
| `TEMPLATE_SHIPPED` | the file is in `assets/data/sections/` and its `template_hash` is recorded | any edit | to `TEMPLATE_DRAFT` (new `template_hash`; saves before the first external build are disposable, SL-14) | the author only; never at runtime (LY-2) |

**Authored subjects (initial state written here; transitions owned elsewhere).**

| Subject | State | Entry condition | Exit condition | Transitions | Who may cause them |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Fault (live or dead) | `LATENT` | held by a lever at build: a closed valve (flow only, DA-16), an open breaker, a thin margin, an absent load, or an absent weld | the lever is released | to `ACTIVE` when the player or the weld releases it; PWR-OVL on installing a heater; O2-ROOM on the weld | the player (V3, V5, install, V9); Assembly (the weld) |
| Fault | `DRIED` | unserved at build, `intensity_pm` 0, `since_steps` at least `DRIED_AFTER_STEPS` `[PLACEHOLDER: Failure & Trail]` | power or coolant reaches it | to `ACTIVE`; a non-leaky dead fault is otherwise stable, a leaky one wears (DA-17) | the player feeding the branch; the Graph's wear |
| Fault | `ACTIVE` | `intensity_pm` above 0; joins the glow count | the Graph's mode machine | to the Graph's DEGRADED, FAILED, DESTROYED, PATCHED states (the Graph's, not Authoring's) | the Graph (endogenous); the player (patch, repair, close a valve) |
| Residual lamp | `LIT` | island battery stock above 0, lamp `switch_on` true | stock reaches 0 | to `DRAINED` while the section is loaded; the lamp dims for one step and goes dark, it never fades for effect | the Graph (D.6 draw); a Suit top-up withdrawal shortens it step for step |
| Residual lamp | `DRAINED` | battery stock 0 | the tie is closed on a powered bus | to `CHARGING`; otherwise none | the player closing the tie junction (V3) with the bus served |
| Residual lamp | `CHARGING` | tie closed, bus served by a source (B only; on A the tie merges the batteries, D.16, and `NO_SOURCE` applies) | stock at its cap, or the tie opens | back to `LIT` as stock rises; recharge at `min(S - served, CH_CAP)` per step (D.6) | the player; the Graph |
| Wreck bus (A, B) | `DEAD` | build state: junction open or broken (A), reactor SCRAMmed (B) | the junction is replaced or patched and closed (A); V12 restarts the reactor (B) | to `WOKEN`: lanterns come on, dormant faults emit, the DERELICT clock applies to the loaded section | the player (swap breaker, V12, V3) |
| Door | `CLOSED` / `OPEN` | `area` 0 or `area_max` at build per the room tables | the player or an opening event | between the two (the Graph's `area` and `door_state`, Layout's leaf presentation); `cut` and `welded` leaf states are not used on interior doors in MVP (DA-8) | Interaction (`set_opening_area`, M13); the Graph |
| Socket | `FREE` | build state (the only MVP sockets are `sock_airlock_e`, `sock_b_w`) | the weld | `FREE` to `WELDED` to `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`, never back (Layout's `socket_state`) | Assembly's atomic apply, through Layout's LM2 `attach_section` and LM3 `detach_section` (Assembly is on disk, In Design) |
| Section load | `LOADED` / `DORMANT` | built and loaded / not loaded | load or unload | the Graph skips a dormant section's slots (LS-17); `can_join` returns `SECTION_NOT_LOADED` | Web Map & Transit (provisional — undesigned); not Authoring |
| Loose item | `PLACED` | seeded by `place_loose` at world build | picked up | to carried (Interaction's holder) and back by a drop | Interaction; Authoring owns only the initial placement |
| Module node | at its authored `hp` | built | cut free, installed, patched, repaired, destroyed | the Graph and Interaction's modules lifecycle (M6, M7, M5) | the player; the Graph |

A section's template state, a body's pose and a fault's mode are three different things: this GDD writes the first and the *initial* value of the last, and owns neither a transition nor a hash.


### Interactions with Other Systems

**Authoring registers no hook, no state block, no mutator and no read_view (DA-1).** Every interface below is the consumer's or the provider's; `data in` means what Authoring reads to write or lint its files, `data out` means what Authoring's files supply. Disk status (Glob of `design/gdd/`, 2026-10-26, at the time this part was written): designed — kernel, Graph, Item DB, Controller, Pipeline, Emitter, 2D Lighting, Failure & Trail, Save/Load, Suit, Interaction, Ship Section & Layout, Ship Body & Interior Physics, Attention; **on disk, In Design (refreshed 2026-10-27)** — Modular Ship Assembly (159 KB; it names this GDD 14 times and its C11 flags the Assembly row below as wrong on ownership, now corrected); **on disk since 2026-10-26 (rows refreshed 2026-10-27 where an ask arrived)** — Boarding & Salvage, Web Map & Transit, Horror Entities, Sanity, Perception Filter, In-World Instruments, Chart Table, Adaptive Audio, HUD, Debug Overlay; **no file** — Procedural Derelict Generation, Environmental Storytelling, Onboarding. Every contract with a system in the last group is marked `(provisional — X undesigned/in flight)` and says what that GDD must repeat.

#### Upstream (this GDD depends on them)

- JSON parsing (`JSON.parse_string` returns floats; cast and bound-check ints): LOW (older API; GDD flags `[UNV]` float behaviour in 4.7.2 spike).
